# Adapt an interface to a new context

Identify the source and target environments, including the task, input methods, viewport,
orientation, and network assumptions. Keep the primary task and its recovery paths available in
both. For native apps, use the project's platform conventions and controls.

Choose breakpoints where the content or interaction stops working. On a narrow screen, put the
main action and its prerequisites in reading order. Move secondary information behind accessible
disclosure only if users can still discover and reach it. Controls that reveal information on
hover need a touch and keyboard path as well. On wide screens, constrain text measure and retain
the order of the workflow when panels sit side by side.

Verify the primary task at the target sizes and at the points between layouts. Include long text,
zoom, touch, and keyboard interaction where applicable. For print or email, check the delivered
format separately and preserve the information needed without interactive controls.
